name: Billund Airport
before:
Denmark's second airport, just outside Billund, and one of the country's busiest cargo centres as well as a charter destination. It carries more than three million passengers a year and is tenth busiest in the Nordic countries.

The Lego connection is not a coincidence. The airport began in 1961 as a private 800 metre runway and hangar built by Godtfred Kirk Christiansen, son of the Lego Group's founder, north of his factory. Neighbouring municipalities joined as owners, a proper airport was built during 1964 and it opened that November. Passengers were handled in Lego's own hangar until the first terminal opened in spring 1966, and Lego's former chief pilot became its first director.

Road distances are worth knowing when placing a client: Vejle is 28 km, Kolding 41 km, Esbjerg 61 km and Aarhus 98 km. Airport buses serve all of those plus Horsens, Skanderborg and Give.

The main runway takes aircraft as large as a 747, though almost all 747 movements here are freight.
after:
Denmark's second airport, just outside Billund. It is one of the country's busiest cargo centres as well as a charter destination, and carries more than three million passengers a year.

Opened in 1964 in an old hangar with a single control tower, it is owned by local municipalities.

Airport buses run to Vejle, Kolding, Give, Esbjerg, Horsens, Skanderborg and Aarhus, connecting with trains.
